input.task: What is the price of the Aurora Desk Lamp?

provenance: Cold review of M42, finding 1 (HIGH), and the milestone's worst defect. `execute`'s extract branch appended to `extractions` and `answers` and THEN raised the identity-anchor check — harmless for five milestones because mode B ends the run at the first failed step, so nothing ever read what a failed step had already written. Loop mode makes a failed call routine, and the refused read stayed in `answers`: `status: success`, `answer: 'Nimbus Wall Clock'`, verdict PASS, with the trace carrying `failure_class: 'semantic'` on the very step the answer came from — a run reporting success alongside its own refutation. No verifier predicate could catch it: nothing in `verify` keys on `failure_class`, `no_failed_postcondition` reads `postcondition_ok is False` (a raise inside `execute` leaves it None) and `actions_verified` covers only state-changing verbs. The fix is a rollback in `attempt`, not a reordering of that one check: any step that fails after writing evidence has the same shape, and the URL guard that fires AFTER `execute` returns is the second instance. A model-authored `anchor` missing the page byte-for-byte is the ordinary case, not an exotic one — the tool schema asks for an anchor on every extract. First written against a link name shop.html does not carry, so it passed on a locate failure without ever reaching the ordering it exists to pin — recorded because a case that goes green for the wrong reason is the failure mode this repo watches reds to avoid.

triage.note: INV-2's shape, reached through a path the verifier structurally cannot see
